deities: Goddess Kunjapuri (Devi; Sati/Durga) - the presiding deity
festivals: Navratri (April and October - the biggest celebrations, thousands of pilgrims)

history.dynasty: None (mythological antiquity; one source credits foundation to Jagadguru Shankaracharya - weakly sourced, verify)
history.period: Antiquity unknown (mythological origin; no documented construction date)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: Kunjapuri Temple is NOT in Rishikesh town - it stands atop the 1,676-metre Kunjapuri hill near Narendra Nagar in Tehri Garhwal district, about 7 km from Narendra Nagar and 25-27 km by road from Rishikesh. It is one of the Siddha Peethas / Shakti Peethas of Uttarakhand (one of 51/52 per various sources): tradition says the chest of the goddess Sati fell here, and it forms a sacred triangle with the Surkanda Devi and Chandrabadani temples. The shrine is a famous sunrise viewpoint over the Garhwal Himalayan peaks (Swarga Rohini, Gangotri, Banderpunch, Chaukhamba) and the Doon Valley. Sources conflict on daily timings (5 AM-6 PM, 5 AM-7 PM, and 6 AM-8 PM are all cited - verify locally); no entry fee. Documented with the corrected location; no reliable construction-era evidence exists, so the antiquity claim is flagged rather than asserted.

name: Kunjapuri Temple
town: Narendra Nagar (CSV town 'Rishikesh' is approximate - the temple is ~25 km from Rishikesh on the Narendra Nagar route)
town_description: Narendra Nagar, founded in the early 20th century as the capital of the Tehri princely state, is a small town in Tehri Garhwal district at about 1,326 m, overlooking Rishikesh and the Doon Valley. It is a quiet base for yoga retreats and Himalayan viewpoints, with the Kunjapuri hill and its Shakti temple about 7 km away.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun - about 38 km.
travel.railway: Rishikesh Railway Station - about 25-27 km by road.
travel.road: About 25-27 km from Rishikesh (approx. 1 hour) and 7 km from Narendra Nagar; reachable by taxi. About 80-300 steps (accounts vary) climb from the road to the shrine.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November for clear skies and sunrise views; Navratri (April/October) for the major celebrations. Avoid July-August monsoon rains.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 5:00 AM - 6:00 PM, 5:00 AM - 7:00 PM, and 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM are all cited (verify locally). No entry fee.
